title: Push Register — payload
description: A device registers its platform push token (APNs / FCM / Web Push) with a push gateway and names who controls the resulting handle's trigger allowlist: a controller VTA (`controllerVtaDid`), or — where the gateway's policy admits it — the device itself (`selfControl`), with its own initial allowlist. Exactly one of the two. The gateway returns an opaque WakeHandle; the raw token is held by the gateway only. See the push wake-up binding (https://trusttasks.org/binding/push/0.1).

registration.description: The platform push channel (token). Held by the gateway only — never disclosed to any other party.

controllerVtaDid.description: The DID of the VTA permitted to provision this handle's trigger allowlist (push/provision). The device conveys the resulting handle to this VTA via device/set-wake. Absent when `selfControl` is present.

selfControl.description: The device controls this handle itself: the gateway records the registering device's authenticated DID as the controller and starts the handle with the allowlist given here. Admitted only where the gateway's policy allows self-controlled handles. Absent when `controllerVtaDid` is present.

SelfControl.title: SelfControl
SelfControl.description: A self-controlled handle's initial trigger allowlist. The device names the parties it allows to wake it — typically its own mediator, the only party that knows when mail is queued for it and it is offline.

allowedTriggers.description: DIDs permitted to trigger a wake for this handle. Empty: nobody, until the device provisions a list (push/provision). The device MUST NOT name itself.

wakeHandle.description: The opaque gateway-issued handle (gateway address + handle). Conveyed onward; reveals no token.
